content.text:
I checked all six problems against the code on jusprin-dev and against the real Ollama 0.40.18 on this Mac. All six are real. I haven't changed any code yet. Three of the fixes show a new sentence, so they need your yes. The other three use only words that are already approved, or the other side's own words.

**1. A local model's own error is reported as ours.** Someone chats with a model in Ollama, and Ollama refuses the request. Maybe the model was deleted (Ollama answers 404: "model 'no-such-model:1b' not found", which I saw on this Mac), or it's too big for memory (500: "llama runner process has terminated"). Today the person sees "Something went wrong on our side", and we get a report. The failure is theirs. **Fix:** show Ollama's own words in the existing format, for example: Ollama says: "model 'x' not found". No report. This also covers the same refusal during the model check in Preferences, and LM Studio's errors when they come in the same form.

**2. A wrong address or an older Ollama is reported as ours.** Someone enters port 5000. On a Mac, something else answers there with 403 and an empty body. Today that's "Something went wrong on our side". **Fix:** any answer that isn't Ollama or LM Studio talking shows the approved sentence: "Nothing is answering at <address>. Start Ollama or LM Studio, then try again." One limit: someone running an Ollama too old to have the chat endpoint gets this sentence too, and it doesn't tell them to update. I'd accept that rather than add a fourth sentence.

**3. A failed save while switching profile opens our report dialog.** Someone has the cut tool open and picks another printer or filament. The app must save a version before dropping their setting changes. The save refuses because a tool is open, and they're told "Something went wrong on our side", though closing the tool fixes it. **Fix:** stop the switch and show a new sentence. When the AI made the switch, the AI is told instead and asks the person to close the tool. Save failures that really are ours are reported once, by the code that started the work: no dialog during an AI tool call, and one window instead of two when opening a project.

**4. A timed-out setup command is recognised only in English.** Someone connects an outside AI app such as Claude Code, and its command runs past 30 seconds. In English they're told that settings might have changed and shown the file. In German or any other language the app looks for the English words "timed out" and doesn't find them. So it shows "Copy the command and run it yourself" and drops the warning. **Fix:** the command passes back a timed-out flag, and the app checks the flag. No wording changes.

**5. A chat too long for the model gives no next step.** Today it says "The request was too large for the <service> service." **Fix:** a new sentence that says to start a new chat.

**6. An outage at the person's own AI service reads like a network problem.** OpenAI, OpenRouter or Anthropic answers 500 or more, or reports an overload mid-reply. The person sees "The AI request could not reach the <service> service", the same sentence they'd see with no network, so they go and check their own connection. **Fix:** a new sentence that puts the trouble at the service. Retry stays available. A key check that hits an outage still says nothing about whether the key is good.

**Decision needed:** do you approve these three new sentences? Each will have translations in JusPrin's own catalogs and a test.
- For the save refused because a tool is open (problem 3): "An editing tool is open. Close it, then try again."
- For the chat too long (problem 5): "This chat is too long for the <service> service. Start a new chat to continue." This also covers a chat with too many pictures, where a new chat is also the way out.
- For the outage (problem 6): "The <service> service is having trouble right now. Try again later." This is the audit's wording, and I'd keep it.

You can approve them, or give your own wording for any of them. Once you confirm, I'll reproduce each problem, fix it in a new worktree from `origin/jusprin-dev`, and commit one fix or one small group of related fixes per commit, quoting your words wherever a sentence needed your yes. I won't push without asking you.

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

commit e8aee03faf2c60a10d687cba1dfa64715fdd1369
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 25 10:51:21 2026 -0800

    A refusal from a person's own AI service is shown in the service's words; outages, an offline sign-out and unreadable shipped profiles go to whoever can act on them
    
    These places sent a failure to the wrong one, by the Error handling rules in
    AGENTS.md. Each was made to happen in the built app before it was changed, and
    again after.
    
    A person's own AI service refuses and says why. JusPrin 2.0.1 answered
    "Something went wrong on our side" and sent us a report nobody here could act
    on. The report that started this work came from the key check: a person's
    OpenRouter workspace took only their own provider keys, and OpenRouter
    answered 404 with words that said what to do and gave the address. The app
    now shows the other side's own words after its name, in one line of text:
    
        OpenRouter says: “No endpoints found that can be served by your own
        provider keys. … Add provider keys at https://openrouter.ai/…”
    
    Kenneth approved the form on 2026-11-24: "Name, then its words". The words
    stay in the language they came in, and only the message text is shown. The
    line is one translatable string, translated in the 22 catalogs.
    
    It is shown in three places, and none of them is reported:
    - The key check in Preferences and in first-run setup, for any refusal that
      carries words. The key check sends the same request for every person; only
      the key and its account differ.
    - A chat on a person's own key, for a 403 that carries words (a country the
      service does not serve, a spending limit, input its moderation flagged) and
      for a 429 that carries words, which can name a daily cap. A 429 with no
      words keeps "The <service> service is rate limited. Try again shortly."
      A 400, 404 or 422 on a chat stays ours: we build that request, and a
      malformed one cannot be told from a refusal.
    - Exporting kept G-code from Print history into a folder the system refuses,
      such as a locked or full card. The app used to report it as ours and show
      nothing. It now shows "macOS says: “/Volumes/CARD: Read-only file system”"
      under "Couldn't export G-code". A failure about any other path is still
      ours.
    
    The AI service behind a person's own key is down or overloaded. The app said
    "Something went wrong on our side" and sent us a report on every try, and
    again for the chat's title and for the models list. Nobody here can fix that
    service. An answer of 500 or above, and an overload or server error named
    inside a reply (Anthropic's overloaded_error and api_error, OpenAI's
    server_error, OpenRouter's provider_overloaded, provider_unavailable and
    server), now shows the sentence the app already has, "The AI request could not
    reach the <service> service.", with its retry, and is not reported. A JusPrin
    account is unchanged: that service is ours, and its failures still come to us.
    A model on this computer is unchanged too.
    
    Signing out with no network. The token is already forgotten on this computer
    and there is nothing for anyone to do, but the failed revoke was reported as
    ours. No answer at all is now logged only. An error answer from our server is
    still ours and still reported.
    
    The printer profiles shipped with the app cannot be read. The printer setup
    form showed "The printer profiles could not be read:" with the loader's
    English error and a file path. A person cannot change files inside the app;
    this happens only on a broken install, which is ours. The loader now throws,
    and the printer chat's handler reports it. That sentence is gone from the
    source and the catalogs. SetupOptions::error is now never set; the form still
    carries the field.
    
    Entire-Checkpoint: 01M8A6QJ4DM5J0E06VKNBEHEFR

# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

# JusPrin's translations

JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for
(`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's
catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own
text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never
conflicts in a translation file:

| Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL`, `translated_plural` | `native/<lang>.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`, the catalog the app loads |
| The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/<lang>.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) |

Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of
`native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used.

Text the fork takes from upstream before upstream's catalogs have it, such as
a cherry-picked fix with a new message, would reach the person in English.
`update_catalogs.py` also reads the OrcaSlicer files listed in its
`UPSTREAM_AHEAD`; their text missing from OrcaSlicer's template becomes JusPrin
entries, and leaves again once upstream's template has it. Add a file there
when taking such a change, and remove it once upstream's catalogs carry its
text.

## Updating the catalogs

After marking or changing text:

```bash
python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py
```

It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the
pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new
entry in every `<lang>.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's
`AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line
break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine
translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: <what>` where
the meaning or the wording is uncertain. `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails
while any entry is untranslated or a translation loses a placeholder.

The page catalogs use ICU placeholders: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags like
`<0>…</0>` for elements inside a `Trans`, and
`{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` for counts. Keep the
placeholder and tag names; translate the words, including the words inside a
plural's branches, and give the plural the categories the language uses
(`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`).

## Marking text

Mark every string a person reads: labels, buttons, headings, menu items,
tooltips, `aria-label`s, placeholders, empty states, confirmation and error
text. Do not change the English: marking must leave the source text exactly
as it was.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs the clang-tidy check that gates pull requests (.github/workflows/clang_tidy.yml)
# on your branch, so its findings match what CI reports. Linux and macOS.
#
#   scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh            check your changes against OrcaSlicer's main
#   scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh --fix      also add the missing includes it names
#
# It configures a separate build directory (build-tidy) without the precompiled
# header, uses the clang-tidy on your system or installs the pinned one into a
# virtual environment inside it, and runs scripts/clang_tidy_diff.py the way CI
# does. Uncommitted changes are checked too.
set -euo pipefail
usage() {
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage: scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh [options]
  -b, --base REV       revision to compare against (default: main of the remote that
                       points at OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer, else origin/main)
      --no-fetch       do not fetch that remote's main first
  -B, --build-dir DIR  build directory for the compile database (default: build-tidy)
  -d, --deps-dir DIR   dependency build directory (default: deps/build on Linux,
                       deps/build/<arch> on macOS)
  -j, --jobs N         parallel clang-tidy runs (default: all cores)
      --fix            apply clang-tidy's fixes (adds the missing includes)
  -y, --yes            install missing tools without asking; another clang-tidy
                       version found on the system is then not offered
  -h, --help           show this help
EOF
}
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
cd "$ROOT"

A model on this computer refusing in its app's own words is shown to the person, and a wrong address is no longer reported as ours

These failures went to the wrong one, by the Error handling rules in
AGENTS.md. Each was made to happen in the host tests before it was changed,
with Ollama 0.40.18's real answers taken on this Mac on 2026-11-25, and again
after.

Ollama refuses a request and says why. A model deleted since setup makes it
answer 404 "model 'qwen3.5:9b' not found"; a model too big for the memory
makes it answer 500 "llama runner process has terminated". A chat showed
"Something went wrong on our side" and sent us a report; the Preferences
check of a model did the same for a 500 and for a refusal while listing or
describing the models. The person can act on these, so the app now shows
the app's own words after its name, in the form Kenneth approved on
2026-11-24 ("Name, then its words"), and sends no report:

    Ollama says: “model 'qwen3.5:9b' not found”

The name is the app setup found, Ollama or LM Studio, and the address when
setup could not tell (as for any other app with a Responses endpoint). The
code is local_refused. Ollama's own API puts its words in the error itself
